PART V  Medical Nutrition Therapy 
HIV is transmitted via direct contact with infected body 
fluids such as blood, semen, preseminal fluid, vaginal fluid, 
and breast milk. Cerebrospinal fluid surrounding the brain 
and spinal cord, synovial fluid surrounding joints, and am-
niotic fluid surrounding a fetus are other fluids that can 
transmit HIV. Saliva, tears, and urine do not contain enough 
HIV for transmission. Sexual transmission is the most com-
mon way HIV is transmitted, and injection drug use is 
the second most prevalent method of transmission (see 
Figure 37-2).
Most people have HIV-1 infection, which, unless speci-
fied, is the type discussed in this chapter. HIV
